title: Calendar Fragmentation Score
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=calendar:event
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as meetings, sum(duration_min) as total_minutes, dc(calendar_name) as calendars by _time
| eval fragmentation=round(meetings+calendars+(total_minutes/60),1)
| where meetings>6
| sort - fragmentation
description: Builds a rough fragmentation score for days full of short meetings and calendar context switching instead of large blocks of protected time.
value: Many productive days fail because they are chopped into unusable pieces; this metric turns that feeling into something measurable.
implementation: Forward calendar events with duration and source calendar; review high-fragmentation days and protect bigger blocks next week.
visualization: Daily chart of meeting count, duration, and fragmentation score.
grandmaExplanation: It watches which days got chopped up into so many meetings and calendar slices that focused work was hard.
